answer.rationale: Write-path p99 has climbed for 90 minutes starting after a release that shipped 2 hours ago, which matches a staged/canary regression more closely than a pure load cliff. memory_b6 says canaries have surfaced bad builds within an hour; memory_b1 says rollback cleared a prior spike with a stable previous build and no customer-write loss. Peak settlement writes are a real confounder (memory_b3), so this is not treated as proven causation. Circuit breakers risk dropping customer writes; read-replica routing addresses report/read load, not this write path; failover has no regional signal. Rollback is the single intervention that can restore a known-good write path. Settlement is at daily peak, so downstream settlement value is flagged and the rollback should stay scoped rather than an unguarded broad cutover. Cause remains uncertain until the two archives are checked.
